name: boxes
why: Draws ASCII boxes around text with hundreds of templates, a pleasant curiosity but close to pretty-output territory.

brief.what_it_is: Boxes is a command-line program that draws, removes, and repairs ASCII art boxes around text. It works as a text filter: text goes in, and the same text comes out wrapped in a box sized to fit it. Boxes can be open on any side, and designs can use UTF-8 characters and colors. Its templates are plain configuration entries, and the homepage says users can add their own by appending to a free-format config file.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to make function headers in source code look better, to decorate news postings, emails and documentation, and to add boxes from scripts because the box matches the input size. It also says open-sided boxes can serve as regional comments in any programming language.
brief.how_it_works: Boxes is a text filter that reads text on stdin and writes the boxed result. Because the box is matched to the content's size, it can be re-run to resize or repair a box that has been damaged by edits to the text inside. Command-line options control how the text sits inside the box, and regular expressions can change the text when a box is added or removed.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a Download/Install section, but I did not follow it to the Download or Usage pages, so I have no install steps beyond the brew formula. The homepage also says Boxes integrates into text editors, with a separate guide.
brief.standout: Most ASCII box tools draw one fixed frame. Boxes reshapes its frames to fit the content, can remove and repair a box that someone has edited, and lets users define new designs in a plain config file. The brew scout notes call it close to pretty-output territory, but the homepage positions it as a tool for code comments and scripting, not just decoration.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage lists v2.3.2 released Aug 29, 2026 with multiple fixes across systems, and v2.3.1 released Oct 3, 2024 with a Windows bug fix. The site has a What's New page and a Release History link. I did not check a git repository for recent commits.
brief.caveats: I only read the homepage, so the manual, config syntax, and template list are unchecked. The brew scout note calls it a curiosity close to pretty-output territory; that is the scout's view, not something the homepage says. Licensed under GPLv3, per the homepage. The homepage does not mention platform limits, but the v2.3.1 release notes mention older Windows variants.
quotes: Boxes is a command line program which draws, removes, and repairs ASCII art boxes.
Since boxes may be open on any side, boxes can also be used to create (regional) comments in any programming language.
New box designs of all sorts can easily be added and shared by appending to a free format configuration file. Be creative!
